key_decisions: No polkit: PAM handshake per session (daemon-side, service ursine, wheel check) then RAM-only Bearer session token. Web moves to OIDC later without API changes.
No database, daemon stateless: system is source of truth (apk/flatpak/nix/shadow/btrfs). Audit = JSONL + logrotate. Config = /etc/ursine/config.toml, tri-state auto|true|false.
Capabilities runtime-detected, never persisted; ensure_available() per request; capabilities.refresh + config.init APIs.
asUser param for per-user ops (flatpak --user, nix profile); default = principal; apk/--system always root.
Cargo features web/oidc trim binary (~2-3 MB) and idle RSS (~3-6 MB target); daemon always on via dinit, event-driven, no polling.
Modules v1: packages (nix first — unique gap), snapshots (owned by packages/store: manual + pre-update auto), users (accountsservice), niri config editor.
Do NOT build printers/scanners/bluetooth/network/firewall/disks — already packaged on Alpine (see docs/PROJECT.md).
Rust everywhere: GUI must be gtk4-rs/libadwaita (Wayle stack) anyway; shared serde types make a second backend language a liability.

Build policy: musl everywhere incl. nix (pkgsMusl/pkgsStatic, never glibc). Local builds via Docker + Alpine images (rust:alpine). CI: test every cargo feature combination; build and publish nix flake (repo-resident, github:skea999/ursine; Release artifacts on tag).
Agents wired: opencode.json instructions load CONTEXT/architecture/PROJECT/handoff/TASKS into every agent; .opencode/rules/ursine.md holds binding project invariants (via opencode-rules plugin).

INTENT CONFIRMED: version plan v1 (backend+GUI: nix, users, snapshots, niri) / v2 (apk, flatpak, printers, scanners, bluetooth, network, firewall, disks) / v3 (OIDC + web, LAST frontend) / v4 (Incus UI) / v5 (ZFS + Pirateus) / v6 (other distros). Phasing != exclusion: everything is in scope.

UI principles (binding): all UIs must look as similar as possible (one design language, same layout/navigation/icons/terminology, libadwaita-aligned theme) and must be user-friendly (HIG compliance, capability-gated panels never shown broken, confirm destructive actions, plain language).
